issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse: problem statement UML declares a private method singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal) (takes an Animal parameter). The template implementation declares the method without a parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)) which comments out the parameter. The solution implements protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (accepts an Animal). This parameter mismatch (template missing the Animal parameter while UML and solution expect it) will cause compilation/signature mismatches and prevents students from following the UML or the solution method contract.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Farm.singFarmSongVerse signature to accept an Animal parameter: e.g. private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (or protected if following solution visibility) and update the method body to use that parameter. This aligns the template with the UML and the solution and avoids compilation/signature mismatches.

issues.description: Visibility of Farm.singFarmSongVerse: the UML/problem statement indicates singFarmSongVerse is private ( '-' in the UML ) and the template declares it private (private void singFarmSongVerse(...)). The solution uses protected visibility (protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). This inconsistency about access level (private vs protected) can confuse students about whether the helper should be accessible to subclasses or only internal to Farm.
issues.suggestedFix: Make visibility consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's singFarmSongVerse to private to match the UML/template if it should be strictly internal, or (B) update the UML and the template to declare the method as protected if subclass access is intended. Prefer option B only if helper access from subclasses is required; otherwise prefer keeping it private. Ensure all three artifacts (UML/problem statement, template, solution) use the same visibility.
